title: A statistical and numerical modeling approach for spatiotemporal reconstruction of glaciations in the Central Asian mountains
author: Saha, Owen, et al.

steps.title: Obtain and prepare climate datasets
steps.instruction: Download CRU CL 2.0 temperature data (10′ latitude/longitude) from https://crudata.uea.ac.uk/cru/data/hrg/tmc/ and TRMM precipitation data (4‑km horizontal × 250‑m vertical) from http://www.geog.ucsb.edu/~bodo/TRMM/. Load both datasets into ArcGIS 10.5.

steps.title: Rescale climate rasters to 18 km grid
steps.instruction: In ArcGIS 10.5, resample the temperature and precipitation rasters to a uniform 18 × 18 km grid cell for each month.

steps.title: Average climate data over years
steps.instruction: Compute monthly averages of the rescaled temperature raster over a 30‑year period and of the precipitation raster over a 12‑year period. (Do not use CRU CL 2.0 precipitation reanalysis because of high uncertainties at high altitude.)

steps.title: Convert glacier polygons to points
steps.instruction: Download the Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI 6.0) containing ~42,511 glacier polygons. In ArcGIS 10.5 use the ‘Feature to Point’ tool to convert each polygon to a point located at its centroid.

steps.title: Extract climate values for each glacier point
steps.instruction: Using the ‘Extract Multi Values to Points’ tool in ArcGIS 10.5, extract the monthly temperature and precipitation values from the averaged rasters for every glacier point.

steps.title: Calculate nine climate parameters
steps.instruction: For each glacier (point) compute the following parameters using the extracted monthly data:

substeps.instruction: Annual temperature range: ΔT(x) = T_max(x) – T_min(x)
Annual precipitation range: ΔPCP(x) = PCP_max(x) – PCP_min(x)
Seasonality Concentration Index: SCI = (1/12) ∑_{i=1}^{12} [ (PCP_i(x) – PCP̅)² / PCP̅² ] where PCP̅ is mean annual precipitation
Relative Entropy: RE = ∑_{m=1}^{12} PCP_m(x) log₂[ 12 · PCP_m(x) / PCP ] where PCP_m(x)=PCP_i(x)/PCP
Dimensionless Seasonality Index: DSI = RE · PCP_R where R is the maximum of ∑_{i=1}^{12} PCP_i(x) among all glaciers (see Supplementary Table S1)

steps.title: Scale parameters to 0‑1 range
steps.instruction: For all parameters except DSI, divide each value by the maximum value of that parameter across the entire glacier sample to obtain a scaled value between 0 and 1 (e.g., T(x)/T_max).
